Critical activities involve the synthesis of novel receptors. The intensive and extensive use of water in modern society places increasing demands on water supplies. This situation negatively impacts fresh water fit for human consumption and agricultural usage as well as the need in industry. Sustainable practices that either enable the removal of chloride from water or enable the performance of industrial processes even in chloride-laden waters are needed. Traditional approaches use reverse osmosis (RO) and electrodialysis across membranes, ion exchange with resin beads, or simple distillation. Despite advances in anion recognition chemistry, none of them use these principles, e.g., RO membranes leverage polyamide films that act as a size filter. This project seeks to take some of the first steps to leverage anion recognition chemistry for chloride sequestration and sensing in polymer materials. This postdoctoral scholar position involves the synthesis of new and known chloride-binding macrocycles and proof-of-concept testing of their ability to extract and sense chloride when incorporated into polymer materials. job_b0e6660c6995c9ee: School of Public Health -Open Rank/Tenure Faculty Position - Biostatistics Bookmark this Requisition Print Preview | Apply for this Job Posting Details Position Information School/College School of Public Health Title School of Public Health -Open Rank/Tenure Faculty Position - Biostatistics Assignment Category Full-Time Rank Open Rank Tenure Status Tenure Track Payroll Status Faculty 12 Job Description The Department of Biostatistics in the School of Public Health (SOPH) at the University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB), is inviting applications from outstanding candidates for multiple full-time tenure-track faculty positions at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor (12-month appointments with rank and tenure status commensurate with qualifications). Faculty will be expected and given the opportunity to develop their own independent line of research. In addition, substantial opportunities to collaborate and publish with other established investigators will be offered. This is an excellent opportunity to expand one’s career into one of the most rapidly progressing and in-demand areas of scientific research. The Department of Biostatistics has 20 faculty members and over 40 administrative and research staff contributing to a diverse portfolio of interdisciplinary projects and academic programs, and is home of the DATA coordinating and Collaborative Research Unit (DATA CRU, https://www.uab.edu/datacru) specializing in the design, data management, and statistical analysis of clinical trials and cohort studies. The Department offers four graduate degrees including the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) and Master of Science (MS), both founded in theory and application. The Doctor of Public Health with concentration in Biostatistics, one of only five programs in the US, and Master of Science in Public Health (MSPH) with concentration in Biostatistics provide a balance between the application of biostatistics and public health theory and leadership. The department also provides courses supporting SOPH undergraduate and graduate degree programs, interdisciplinary graduate degree programs, and the graduate Certificate in Applied Biostatistics and Epidemiology. Founded in 1978, the UAB SOPH has grown to 84 full-time faculty and 806 students (in the 2023-24 academic year). The UAB SOPH is the only CEPH-accredited public health program in Alabama and both the school (18th) and department (13th) are ranked in the top 20 nationally by U.S. News & World Report. The SOPH is second only to the School of Medicine at UAB for extramural research funding among all 12 schools at UAB. In 2023, the UAB SOPH had more than $42 million in grants and contracts and ranked 29th among all Schools of Public Health and 19th for all Public Schools of Public Health for NIH funding. UAB is a very high research activity (R1) university and academic health center that discovers, teaches, and applies knowledge for the intellectual, cultural, social, and economic benefit of Birmingham, the state, and beyond. Spanning more than 100 city blocks, UAB is the state of Alabama’s largest single employer with some 25,000 employees and has an annual, state-wide economic impact exceeding $12.1 billion. Forbes named UAB America’s Best Large Employer for 2021 and best in-state employer in 2023. Applications will be accepted until the positions are filled. Position description UC Davis Tahoe Environmental Research Center (TERC) seeks a Postdoctoral Scholar to conduct interdisciplinary research in lake and aquatic science, hydrodynamic modeling, remote sensing and environmental data science. The successful candidate will investigate the physical processes governing lake circulation and transport of harmful algal blooms through the integration of numerical modeling, field observations, remote sensing products and environmental datasets. The Postdoctoral Scholar will develop, configure, calibrate, and evaluate model predictions for the probability of harmful algal blooms and the transport of algae in lakes and reservoirs. Predictions will be based on combining forecasted and current weather and lake conditions. The successful candidate will also design and execute field experiments, analyze the in-situ observations and model outputs, prepare peer-reviewed publications, present research findings, and coordinate research and outreach activities with agency and stakeholders. The position provides opportunities to lead research associated with developing new numerical models, data processing and analysis, and collaborate across disciplines and agencies. This work will directly contribute to the management and protection of freshwater ecosystems. The Postdoctoral Scholar will report directly to the Project’s Principal Investigators Alexander Forrest, Sergio Valbuena, and Oscar Sepulveda.
